text: I'm not going to lie to you. The ovens hummed their low lullaby. Yeast, burnt sugar. I wiped flour off my forearms, checked the clock. 3:17 AM. Thursday. The bookstore was dead. No customers. I walked to the front counter and found a paperback sitting on the glass display case. The Shadow of the Wind. It had been there six weeks. Every night I'd toss it in the return bin, assume some confused person left it in the bakery's late-night drop slot thinking it was a library return. But tonight it was different. The book was warm, not the cool air of the shop. Picked it up. Opened it to the bookmarked page. A folded square of notebook paper fell out. Unfolded. Jagged, hurried writing. I know you're reading it. Keep going. Page 204 changes everything. Heart pounding, hammering against my ribs. Sharp rhythm against the quiet hum of the mixers. Looked around the empty shop. Shadows stretched long across the tiled floor. Nobody there. Back to the note. Back to the book. Trembling fingers, turned to 204. Text blurred. Closed the book, pressed it flat against the counter. Reached for my pen.
